newsitem.title: USA: United to sell Apollo stake for $539 mln.
newsitem.headline: United to sell Apollo stake for $539 mln.

text.p: UAL Corp's United Airlines said Tuesday it reached a non-binding agreement in principle to sell its 77 percent stake in Apollo Travel Services for $539 million to Galileo International Partnership.
In addition, Galileo may pay United up to $154 million more in the sixth year following the sale under a services agreement to help Galileo grow the Apollo business, the company said.

United said the sale is subject to several factors, including the signing of definitive documentation and Galileo's successful completion of an initial public offering. Galileo said IPO proceeds would be used to fund the purchase.

United Chairman and Chief Executive Gerald Greenwald said in a statement the sale would allow United to concentrate on its core competencies, retain its substantial ownership stake in Galileo and realize a major, one-time cash infusion.
"In the long term, United intends to invest the proceeds from the sale of ATS (Apollo) in such a manner as to increase shareholder value by increasing earnings per share," the company said.
United said it does not plan to sell any of its shares in Galileo as part of the IPO and expects to retain a significant ownership percentage after the IPO's completion.
United currently owns about 38 percent of Galileo.
Galileo provides electronic global distribution services for the travel industry. It is owned by an international partnership of 11 airlines, including United.

Apollo is a separate company of which United owns 77 percent, US Airways Group Inc 21 percent and Air Canada two percent. It markets Galileo's Apollo products to about 13,000 travel agencies in the United States, Mexico and the Caribbean.
In addition, Apollo provides network services to United.
Galileo said it said it also agreed to buy US Airways' and Air Canada's stakes in Apollo. It will pay a total of $700 million for Apollo.
United said it will continue to sell Apollo-based products and services in the United States and Mexico after the proposed deal is completed.
